name: Barbell Bench Press
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale on press
coaching_cues: Retract scapula before unrack; 5 contact points; slight diagonal bar path
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows; bouncing bar; losing leg drive
warmup_protocol: 2×10 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: Pause reps 2sec at chest for 4 weeks — adds 10kg to your max fast
indian_alternative: No barbell? Use a loaded backpack for pushup resistance

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale on press
coaching_cues: Neutral or pronated grip; control the stretch; don't let DBs drift wide
common_mistakes: Dropping elbows too low; uneven pressing; wrists bent back
warmup_protocol: 2×12 at 60% with lighter DBs
pro_tip: DB bench gives 30% more range than barbell — use it for hypertrophy phases

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale on press
coaching_cues: 45° incline max; keep elbows at 45° from torso; control descent
common_mistakes: Excessive incline (>45°) shifts load to shoulders; using too heavy weight
warmup_protocol: 2×8 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: Incline DB flyes superset with this — devastating upper chest combo

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale on press
coaching_cues: Head slightly below chest; wider grip than flat; plant feet firmly
common_mistakes: Losing upper back tightness; going too heavy; neck strain
warmup_protocol: 1×10 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: Lower chest is often undertrained — 2 sets here changes your chest shape fast

name: Push Up
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale up
coaching_cues: Hands slightly wider than shoulder width; full body rigid; elbows 45° angle
common_mistakes: Sagging hips; flaring elbows; partial range of motion
warmup_protocol: None needed
pro_tip: Tempo pushups (3sec down) build more chest than fast reps — try 4×10
indian_alternative: Dand (Hindu Pushup) — starts in downward dog, flows through

name: Dumbbell Fly
breathing_cue: Inhale on stretch, exhale on squeeze
coaching_cues: Slight elbow bend throughout; squeeze at top; feel the stretch
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; bending elbows too much (becomes press)
warmup_protocol: 1×15 with very light weight
pro_tip: Stop 10° before full extension — keeps constant tension on chest

name: Cable Fly
breathing_cue: Exhale on squeeze
coaching_cues: Step forward from cables; slight forward lean; meet hands at midline
common_mistakes: Pulling with arms not chest; too much weight; locking elbows
warmup_protocol: 1×15 light weight
pro_tip: Set cables at different heights each set — low, mid, high — for full chest

name: Chest Dip
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale up
coaching_cues: Lean forward 15-20° to hit chest; go below parallel; control descent
common_mistakes: Upright torso (shifts to triceps); flaring elbows wide; rushed reps
warmup_protocol: 2×8 bodyweight
pro_tip: Add 10kg plate once you can do 3×15 — chest dips are highly underrated
indian_alternative: Can use two chairs if no parallel bars

name: Machine Chest Press
breathing_cue: Exhale on press
coaching_cues: Adjust seat so handles are at mid-chest height; keep back flat
common_mistakes: Arching off pad; half reps; wrong seat height
warmup_protocol: None needed
pro_tip: Great for beginners learning chest activation — use before free weights

name: Pike Push Up
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale up
coaching_cues: Hips high in inverted V; lower head between hands; elbows flare slightly
common_mistakes: Flat back position; dropping too fast; incomplete range
warmup_protocol: None needed
pro_tip: Progression toward handstand pushup — essential calisthenics milestone

name: Barbell Overhead Press
breathing_cue: Inhale at top, brace and exhale on press
coaching_cues: Bar from rack at chin height; push bar up and slightly back; lock out overhead
common_mistakes: Forward lean; excessive back arch; not achieving full lockout
warmup_protocol: 2×8 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: Seated OHP vs standing — standing recruits more core but seated allows more load

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
breathing_cue: Inhale at top, exhale on press
coaching_cues: Start at ear level; press slightly arcing inward; full lockout
common_mistakes: Leaning back too much; elbows flaring forward; asymmetrical pressing
warmup_protocol: 1×12 light weight
pro_tip: Arnold press variation adds front delt and rotator cuff activation in one movement

name: Lateral Raise
coaching_cues: Natural breathing
common_mistakes: Slight forward lean; lead with elbows not hands; stop at shoulder height
warmup_protocol: Swinging body; going above shoulder height; too heavy
pro_tip: None needed

name: Face Pull
coaching_cues: Natural breathing
common_mistakes: Pull rope to face level; external rotation at end; elbows above wrists
warmup_protocol: Too much weight; pulling to chest not face; no external rotation
pro_tip: None needed

name: Front Raise
coaching_cues: Exhale on raise
common_mistakes: Slight elbow bend; stop at shoulder height; control descent
warmup_protocol: Swinging; going too high; too heavy weight
pro_tip: None needed

name: Close Grip Bench Press
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale on press
coaching_cues: Hands shoulder width (not too narrow); elbows tucked to sides; full range
common_mistakes: Too narrow grip (wrist strain); flaring elbows out; partial reps
warmup_protocol: 2×8 light weight
pro_tip: Strongest tricep builder — prioritize this over pushdowns for arm size

name: Tricep Pushdown (Cable)
coaching_cues: Exhale on pushdown
common_mistakes: Upper arms locked to sides; full extension at bottom; control return
warmup_protocol: Swinging torso; not locking out; too much weight
pro_tip: None needed

name: Skull Crusher
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale up
coaching_cues: Bar above forehead not nose; upper arms vertical; slight backward angle
common_mistakes: Letting elbows flare out; going too heavy; dropping bar on face
warmup_protocol: 1×12 very light weight
pro_tip: Superset with close grip bench — ultimate tricep finisher. Called 'rolling thunder'.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
breathing_cue: Inhale on stretch, exhale up
coaching_cues: Elbows close to head; full stretch overhead; elbows don't flare
common_mistakes: Elbows splaying out; partial range; going too heavy
warmup_protocol: None needed
pro_tip: Long head of tricep is only fully stretched overhead — essential for arm development

name: Diamond Push Up
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale up
coaching_cues: Form diamond with hands under chest; elbows close to body; full extension
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring out; hips dropping; partial range
warmup_protocol: None needed
pro_tip: One of the best bodyweight tricep builders — can be done anywhere

name: Deadlift
breathing_cue: Big breath and brace before pull, exhale at top
coaching_cues: Bar over mid-foot; hip hinge not squat; engage lats before pulling; push floor away
common_mistakes: Rounding lower back; bar drifting from legs; jerking weight; not bracing
pro_tip: Hook grip eliminates mixed grip imbalances — painful for 2 weeks but worth it for heavy pulls

name: Pull Up
coaching_cues: Inhale at top
exhale on pull
common_mistakes: Dead hang start; depress scapula first; pull elbows to hips; chin over bar
warmup_protocol: Kipping; partial range; not achieving scapular depression; craning neck
pro_tip: 2×5 band assisted

name: Barbell Bent Over Row
breathing_cue: Inhale at bottom, exhale on pull
coaching_cues: Hip hinge 45°; bar to lower chest/upper abs; squeeze at top
common_mistakes: Rounding back; pulling to belly button (upper back miss); using momentum
warmup_protocol: 2×10 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: Overhand vs underhand grip hits different areas — rotate both in your training

name: Dumbbell Row
breathing_cue: Exhale on pull
coaching_cues: Knee on bench; pull DB to hip; elbow skims body; full stretch at bottom
common_mistakes: Rotating torso; short range; pulling to shoulder not hip
warmup_protocol: 1×12 light weight
pro_tip: Kroc rows (high rep, heavy, controlled cheat) build lat thickness no other exercise matches

name: Lat Pulldown
breathing_cue: Exhale on pull
coaching_cues: Slight backward lean; pull to upper chest; elbows drive down and back
common_mistakes: Pulling behind neck; leaning too far back; using momentum; half reps
warmup_protocol: 1×12 light weight
pro_tip: Wide grip hits lat breadth; neutral/close grip hits lat thickness — vary both

name: Seated Cable Row
breathing_cue: Exhale on pull
coaching_cues: Neutral spine; pull to navel; squeeze shoulder blades at top; controlled return
common_mistakes: Rounding back; leaning too far back; pulling too low
warmup_protocol: 1×12 light weight
pro_tip: Pause 1 second at peak contraction every rep — transforms this from good to elite

name: T-Bar Row
breathing_cue: Exhale on pull
coaching_cues: Wide stance; hip hinge; chest on pad; pull to lower chest
common_mistakes: Rounding back; pulling to belly button; too heavy
warmup_protocol: 2×10 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: The ultimate back thickness builder — Dorian Yates built his back on this exercise

name: Hyperextension
coaching_cues: Exhale on extension
common_mistakes: Hips on pad edge; arms crossed on chest; stop at neutral spine
warmup_protocol: Hyperextending past neutral; jerking up; adding weight too soon

name: Chest Supported Row
breathing_cue: Exhale on pull
coaching_cues: Chest on incline bench; elbows flare 45°; squeeze at top
common_mistakes: Using momentum; partial range; going too heavy
warmup_protocol: 1×12 light weight
pro_tip: Chest support eliminates lower back fatigue — great for volume work

name: Barbell Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Upper arms locked to sides; full range; supinate wrist at top; squeeze
common_mistakes: Swinging body; partial range; elbows drifting forward at top
pro_tip: EZ bar reduces wrist strain — switch from straight bar if discomfort

name: Dumbbell Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Alternate arms; supinate wrist during curl; full stretch at bottom
common_mistakes: Swinging; not supinating; rushing reps
pro_tip: Incline DB curl (seated, arms behind torso) gives maximum bicep stretch — try it

name: Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Neutral grip throughout; upper arms fixed; full range
common_mistakes: Swinging; partial range; thumbs pointing out
pro_tip: Brachialis development makes biceps look taller — hammer curls are essential

name: Concentration Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Elbow braced against inner thigh; full range; squeeze at top
common_mistakes: Shifting elbow; using momentum; partial range
pro_tip: Best for the peak contraction of the bicep — end every arm workout with this

name: Cable Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Constant cable tension; upper arms locked; full range
common_mistakes: Elbows drifting forward; using momentum; half reps
pro_tip: Cable gives constant tension barbell cannot — always include 1 cable curl variation

name: Barbell Back Squat
breathing_cue: Big breath and brace before descent, exhale on way up
coaching_cues: Bar on upper traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar); hip width stance; knees track toes; break parallel
common_mistakes: Caving knees; butt wink; heels rising; forward lean
pro_tip: Pause squats — 2sec at bottom — build strength in the hole no other variation matches
indian_alternative: Baithak (Hindu Squat) — continuous breathing squats, 20+ reps, traditional

name: Front Squat
breathing_cue: Brace before descent, exhale on drive
coaching_cues: Elbows high; upright torso; fingertip or cross-arm grip; hip width stance
common_mistakes: Dropping elbows; forward lean; too heavy before mastering technique
warmup_protocol: 2×6 light weight
pro_tip: Best quad builder of any squat variation — prioritize for quad development

name: Goblet Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale up
coaching_cues: Hold weight at chest; elbows inside knees at bottom; upright torso
common_mistakes: Heels rising; not reaching depth; letting weight pull you forward
warmup_protocol: None — self-correcting exercise
pro_tip: Perfect teaching tool for squat pattern — use for warm-up sets at any level

name: Leg Press
breathing_cue: Inhale on descent, exhale on press
coaching_cues: Feet at shoulder width; don't lock knees; controlled descent; don't lift hips
common_mistakes: Locking knees; too much weight; short range of motion; lifting lower back off pad
pro_tip: High feet = more glutes/hamstrings; Low feet = more quads — vary position

name: Hack Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale on drive
coaching_cues: Low foot placement; keep back on pad; full ROM; controlled pace
common_mistakes: Locking knees; partial range; feet too high
warmup_protocol: 1×10 light weight
pro_tip: Low foot placement on hack squat creates one of the best quad isolation stimuli possible

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale down, exhale up
coaching_cues: Back foot elevated on bench; front foot far enough forward; vertical shin
common_mistakes: Front knee caving; leaning too far forward; back foot too high
warmup_protocol: 1×10 BW each side
pro_tip: Arguably better than back squat for hypertrophy — unilateral loading is elite

name: Walking Lunge
breathing_cue: Natural breathing
coaching_cues: Long stride; front knee doesn't pass toes; upright torso; push through heel
common_mistakes: Short stride; knee collapsing; forward lean; rushing
pro_tip: Add dumbbells once 3×20 feels easy — walking lunges are killer for glute development

name: Leg Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale on extension
coaching_cues: Ankle pad above feet; full extension; 1-second squeeze; controlled return
common_mistakes: Going too heavy; partial range; not squeezing at top
pro_tip: Best quad isolation exercise — pair with squats for complete quad development

name: Step Up
breathing_cue: Exhale on step
coaching_cues: Drive through heel of elevated foot; don't push off back foot; upright torso
common_mistakes: Using back leg to push; leaning forward; rushing
pro_tip: Excellent knee-friendly squat alternative for those with knee discomfort

name: Romanian Deadlift
breathing_cue: Inhale on descent, exhale on drive
coaching_cues: Hinge at hip; slight knee bend; bar/DBs close to legs; feel hamstring stretch
common_mistakes: Rounding lower back; squatting the weight; losing bar contact with legs
pro_tip: Control the eccentric (lowering) — 3-4 seconds down is where the growth happens

name: Nordic Curl
breathing_cue: Inhale on descent, exhale on pull
coaching_cues: Ankle secured; slowly lower under control; pull yourself back up
common_mistakes: Rushing the descent; using back to compensate; not going full range
warmup_protocol: Full bodyweight practice sets
pro_tip: Single most effective hamstring injury prevention exercise — elite athletes swear by it

name: Hip Thrust
breathing_cue: Exhale on thrust
coaching_cues: Upper back on bench; drive hips up forcefully; squeeze glutes at top; chin tucked
common_mistakes: Overextending spine; not using glutes; bar rolling; neck strain
pro_tip: Best glute activation of any exercise — use hip thrust before heavy squats as activation

name: Glute Bridge
breathing_cue: Exhale on bridge
coaching_cues: Feet flat on floor; drive hips up; squeeze glutes at top; hold 1sec
common_mistakes: Arching lower back; not squeezing glutes; feet too far from body
pro_tip: Best glute activation warm-up before squats or deadlifts — always start here

name: Leg Curl (Lying)
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Hips flat on pad; full range; squeeze at peak contraction; slow descent
common_mistakes: Lifting hips; short range; going too heavy
pro_tip: Full range leg curls (ankle past knee) activate hamstrings at longer length — better growth

name: Sumo Deadlift
breathing_cue: Big breath before pull, exhale at top
coaching_cues: Wide stance; toes out 45°; vertical shin; hips close to bar; push floor out
common_mistakes: Knees caving; hips rising before shoulders; bar drifting from legs
pro_tip: Sumo removes lower back from equation — good option for those with back issues

name: Standing Calf Raise
breathing_cue: Natural breathing
coaching_cues: Full range — deep stretch at bottom; high rise at top; 2sec pause both ends
common_mistakes: Partial range; bouncing; too fast
pro_tip: Calves need high volume (15-25 reps) and full range to grow — most undertrain them badly

name: Seated Calf Raise
breathing_cue: Natural breathing
coaching_cues: Full range; deep stretch; high rise; pause at top and bottom
common_mistakes: Partial range; bouncing; rushing
pro_tip: Seated targets soleus which gives lower leg thickness — train both seated and standing

name: Donkey Calf Raise
breathing_cue: Natural breathing
coaching_cues: Bent over at 90°; weight on balls of feet; full range
common_mistakes: Partial range; rushing; not using full stretch
pro_tip: Arnold's favourite calf exercise — stretch is greater than standing variation

name: Plank
coaching_cues: Steady breathing throughout
common_mistakes: Forearms or hands; neutral spine; brace hard; don't let hips drop or rise
warmup_protocol: Sagging hips; raised butt; holding breath; neck strain
source: Used in military training — try the RKC variation for rapid core strength

name: Dead Bug
coaching_cues: Exhale as arm/leg extend
common_mistakes: Lower back pressed to floor; opposite arm and leg extend slowly; return with control
warmup_protocol: Lower back arching off floor; moving too fast; holding breath

name: Cable Crunch
breathing_cue: Exhale on crunch
coaching_cues: Kneel facing cable; pull rope to either side of head; curl spine; don't use hips
common_mistakes: Using hips; pulling with arms; partial range
pro_tip: Only weighted ab exercise that truly isolates abs — builds visible six pack definition

name: Hanging Leg Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale on raise
coaching_cues: Dead hang; raise legs to 90° or higher; control descent; don't swing
common_mistakes: Swinging; using momentum; not controlling descent
warmup_protocol: None needed
pro_tip: Tuck version for beginners; straight leg for intermediate; toes to bar for advanced

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
breathing_cue: Inhale on rollout, exhale on return
coaching_cues: Kneel; roll out slowly; hips stay level; pull back using abs not arms
common_mistakes: Hips dropping; too fast; going beyond control
warmup_protocol: Start from knees
pro_tip: The most brutal anti-extension core exercise — face the floor not the wall

name: Russian Twist
breathing_cue: Exhale on rotation
coaching_cues: Lean back slightly; feet off floor; rotate fully both sides; controlled pace
common_mistakes: Half rotation; feet on floor (too easy); rushing
pro_tip: Hold a weight plate for more resistance — core rotation is essential for everyday movement

name: Reverse Crunch
breathing_cue: Exhale on crunch
coaching_cues: Curl hips toward chest; don't swing legs; full range
common_mistakes: Using momentum; swinging; partial range
pro_tip: Hits lower abs that regular crunches completely miss — essential for full ab development

name: Running (Treadmill)
coaching_cues: Nasal breathing at low intensity
mouth at high
common_mistakes: Slight forward lean; midfoot landing; relaxed shoulders; arms at 90°
warmup_protocol: Heel striking; too fast start; hunched shoulders; shallow breathing
pro_tip: 5 min walk
source: Can do on road — early mornings are ideal in Indian summers

name: Cycling (Stationary)
coaching_cues: Steady controlled breathing
common_mistakes: Seat at hip height; slight knee bend at bottom; hands relaxed on bars
warmup_protocol: Seat too low; hunched over; feet pointing down
source: Can use regular cycle outdoors — good morning activity

name: Jump Rope
coaching_cues: Steady breathing
common_mistakes: Land on balls of feet; small jumps; elbows near sides; consistent rhythm
warmup_protocol: Landing hard; rope too long; jumping too high; inconsistent rhythm
pro_tip: 1 min slow
source: One of the cheapest and best cardio tools — available for ₹200 anywhere

name: Rowing Machine
coaching_cues: Exhale on the drive (pull)
common_mistakes: Legs first
then lean back
then pull; reverse on return; keep back straight
warmup_protocol: Pulling with arms first; rounding back; rushing the stroke
pro_tip: 5 min slow rowing

name: Burpee
coaching_cues: Exhale on jump
common_mistakes: Fluid movement; full push up at bottom; explosive jump; hands overhead
warmup_protocol: Half push up; not jumping; sloppy transitions

name: Box Jump
coaching_cues: Exhale on jump
common_mistakes: Quarter squat; explosive arm drive; land softly on box; step down not jump down
warmup_protocol: Landing stiff; not squatting before jump; jumping down (knee strain)
pro_tip: 2×5 at lower box

name: Mountain Climber
coaching_cues: Natural fast breathing
common_mistakes: Push up position; alternate driving knees to chest; hips level
warmup_protocol: Hips rising; too slow; not reaching full knee drive

name: Assault Bike
coaching_cues: Fast breathing at high intensity
common_mistakes: Use both arms and legs; stay seated; consistent pace or HIIT intervals
warmup_protocol: Only using legs; poor posture; starting too hard
pro_tip: 3 min easy cycling

name: Muscle Up
coaching_cues: Exhale on pull and transition
common_mistakes: False grip; explosive pull; transition wrists over bar; press out
warmup_protocol: Insufficient pull up strength; kipping too early; not using false grip
pro_tip: Need 15+ strict pull ups first

name: Front Lever Hold
coaching_cues: Steady controlled breathing
common_mistakes: Grab bar; lift body parallel to floor; straight body; depress scapula
warmup_protocol: Bending knees; hips dropping; bending elbows
pro_tip: Tuck front lever practice

name: L-Sit Hold
coaching_cues: Steady breathing
common_mistakes: Press down on bars/floor; legs parallel to floor; pointed toes; locked knees
warmup_protocol: Bent legs; hips not high enough; bent arms
pro_tip: Tuck L-sit progression first

name: Handstand Hold
coaching_cues: Steady breathing
common_mistakes: Kick up to wall; straight body; squeeze everything; balance on hands
warmup_protocol: Banana back; wide hands; not engaging core
pro_tip: Wall kick-up practice

name: Pistol Squat
coaching_cues: Inhale down
exhale on drive
common_mistakes: One leg extended forward; squat to full depth; arms forward for balance
warmup_protocol: Falling back; knee caving; not reaching depth
pro_tip: Assisted pistol with TRX or band first

name: Dragon Flag
coaching_cues: Inhale on descent
exhale on raise
common_mistakes: Grab bench above head; raise straight body up; lower slowly; don't touch floor
warmup_protocol: Bending at hips; lowering too fast; insufficient strength base
pro_tip: Flat bench leg raise first

name: Dip (Parallel Bars)
coaching_cues: Inhale down
exhale up
common_mistakes: Upright torso for triceps; slight forward lean for chest; full extension
warmup_protocol: Flaring elbows too wide; half reps; not locking out
pro_tip: 2×8 bodyweight

name: Dand (Hindu Pushup)
coaching_cues: Fluid breathing with movement
common_mistakes: Start in downward dog; dive chest forward; cobra at bottom; back to downward dog
warmup_protocol: Breaking the fluid movement; partial range; rushing
source: Core Indian exercise — practiced by wrestlers (pehlwans) for centuries

name: Baithak (Hindu Squat)
coaching_cues: Inhale up to toes
exhale on descent
common_mistakes: Heels rise at bottom; fluid continuous movement; hands swing forward; high rep
warmup_protocol: Breaking rhythm; stopping between reps; too slow
source: Traditional Indian wrestler conditioning — try 100 reps straight

name: Surya Namaskar
coaching_cues: Breath synced with each movement
common_mistakes: 12 positions with coordinated breath; fluid transitions; full range each position
warmup_protocol: Rushing through positions; holding breath; skipping positions
source: Ancient Indian morning practice — complete workout in itself

name: Hip Flexor Stretch
coaching_cues: Deep slow breathing
common_mistakes: Kneeling lunge position; drive hip forward; upright torso; slight posterior tilt
warmup_protocol: Arching lower back; leaning forward; not holding long enough

name: Pigeon Pose
coaching_cues: Deep slow breathing
common_mistakes: Front shin parallel or diagonal; square hips; ease into stretch
warmup_protocol: Forcing the position; collapsing to one side; holding breath

name: Thoracic Extension (Foam Roller)
coaching_cues: Exhale on extension
common_mistakes: Roller perpendicular to spine; hands behind head; extend over roller; move segment by segment
warmup_protocol: Extending lumbar spine; too much pressure; going too fast

name: World's Greatest Stretch
coaching_cues: Deep breathing with each rotation
common_mistakes: Lunge; drop elbow to floor inside foot; rotate thoracic up to sky; extend into hamstring stretch
warmup_protocol: Rushing through sequence; not reaching full rotation

name: Ankle Circles
coaching_cues: Normal breathing
common_mistakes: Seated; lift foot; large slow circles both directions; full range
warmup_protocol: Small circles; rushing; not doing both directions

name: Cat-Cow Stretch
coaching_cues: Inhale on cow (arching)
exhale on cat (rounding)
common_mistakes: On hands and knees; segmental spinal movement; chin to chest on cat; head up on cow
warmup_protocol: Rushing; only moving at extremes; not getting full range

name: Power Clean
coaching_cues: Brace before pull; exhale on catch
common_mistakes: Start like deadlift; explosive triple extension; shrug; pull under bar; catch in front rack
warmup_protocol: Arm-pulling instead of leg drive; early arm bend; poor rack position
pro_tip: Technical coaching required first

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
breathing_cue: Big breath before pull, exhale at top
coaching_cues: Neutral handles; more upright torso than conventional; push floor away
common_mistakes: Squatting the weight; bar drifting; losing back tension
pro_tip: Best of both squat and deadlift — more quad-friendly than conventional, more weight than front squat

name: Zercher Squat
breathing_cue: Brace before descent, exhale on drive
coaching_cues: Bar held in elbow crooks; upright torso; elbows up; hip width stance
common_mistakes: Bar slipping; leaning forward; going too heavy before mastering
warmup_protocol: Practice with light weight first
pro_tip: Forces perfectly upright torso — best squat variation for spinal erector development

name: Farmers Carry
coaching_cues: Natural breathing
brace core
common_mistakes: Heavy weights in each hand; tall posture; short quick steps; shoulders packed
warmup_protocol: Hunching; dragging feet; going too heavy; losing posture

name: Suitcase Carry
coaching_cues: Natural breathing
common_mistakes: Weight one side only; resist lateral lean; tall posture; brace hard
warmup_protocol: Leaning to weighted side; rushing; not bracing core

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift
breathing_cue: Exhale on hinge
coaching_cues: Standing leg slightly bent; hinge at hip; free leg extends back; reach weight toward floor
common_mistakes: Using momentum; rotating hips; losing balance
warmup_protocol: Perform with bodyweight first
pro_tip: Best posterior chain unilateral exercise — reveals left/right imbalances instantly

name: Good Morning
breathing_cue: Inhale on hinge, exhale on return
coaching_cues: Bar on upper back like squat; slight knee bend; hinge to parallel; neutral spine
common_mistakes: Rounding spine; going too heavy; excessive knee bend
warmup_protocol: Start with empty bar
pro_tip: Best posterior chain developer that most people have never tried — elite powerlifters use it

name: Band Pull Apart
coaching_cues: Natural breathing
common_mistakes: Arms straight; pull band to chest; squeeze shoulder blades; controlled return
warmup_protocol: Bending elbows; not fully pulling apart; rushing

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Arms hang behind torso on incline; curl with full stretch; squeeze at top
common_mistakes: Losing the stretch position; swinging; going too heavy
pro_tip: Best bicep peak exercise — the stretch position on an incline is unmatched

name: Preacher Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale on curl
coaching_cues: Upper arms flat on pad; full range; don't throw weight up
common_mistakes: Throwing weight; arms off pad; partial range
pro_tip: Eliminates cheating — great for building the lower bicep thickness

name: Cable Tricep Kickback
breathing_cue: Exhale on extension
coaching_cues: Upper arm parallel to floor; full extension; control return; hinge at hip
common_mistakes: Dropping upper arm; partial extension; using momentum
pro_tip: Forces proper tricep contraction at full extension — great finisher

name: Overhead Tricep Cable Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale on extension
coaching_cues: Face away from cable; elbows close to head; full stretch; full extension
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring; partial range; going too heavy

coaching_cues: Grip bar shoulder-width; let body hang fully; relax shoulders down; engage core slightly
common_mistakes: Shrugging shoulders up; holding breath; swinging
pro_tip: Decompresses spine and builds grip strength — great before any pull exercise

name: Slow Walking
breathing_cue: Slow deep breaths — in through nose, out through mouth
coaching_cues: Walk at a relaxed pace; let heart rate come down gradually; shake out arms gently
common_mistakes: Stopping suddenly after intense exercise; sitting down immediately
pro_tip: Walking after a workout helps clear lactic acid and prevents dizziness

name: Standing Toe Touch
breathing_cue: Exhale as you fold forward, breathe steadily while holding
coaching_cues: Stand with feet together; bend forward from hips; reach for toes; keep knees slightly bent if needed
common_mistakes: Bouncing; rounding upper back excessively; locking knees
pro_tip: Hold for 30 seconds — don't bounce. You'll go deeper with each exhale

name: Standing Quad Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe deeply and steadily while holding
coaching_cues: Stand on one leg; grab opposite foot behind you; pull heel to glute; keep knees together; hold a wall for balance
common_mistakes: Arching lower back; knee pointing outward; not holding long enough
pro_tip: Hold 15 seconds each leg — essential after squats and lunges

name: Overhead Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe deeply, reach higher on each exhale
coaching_cues: Interlace fingers; push palms to ceiling; stretch tall; lean gently to each side
common_mistakes: Not fully extending arms; holding breath; arching lower back
pro_tip: Add a gentle side lean for a lat stretch bonus

name: Side Bend Stretch
breathing_cue: Inhale upright, exhale into the side bend
coaching_cues: Stand tall; raise one arm overhead; lean to the opposite side; hold 15s each side
common_mistakes: Leaning forward instead of sideways; not holding long enough
pro_tip: Keep hips square — feel the stretch along your entire side

name: Cross-body Shoulder Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe deeply while holding the stretch
coaching_cues: Bring one arm across your chest; use opposite hand to press above the elbow; hold 15s each arm
common_mistakes: Pressing on the elbow joint; shrugging the shoulder; rotating the torso
pro_tip: A must-do after any pressing or shoulder workout

name: Chest Doorway Stretch
breathing_cue: Breathe deeply, lean slightly further on each exhale
coaching_cues: Place forearm on a doorframe or wall at 90 degrees; step forward until you feel the chest stretch; hold 15s each side
common_mistakes: Arm too high or too low; arching the lower back; not holding long enough
pro_tip: Counters the rounded posture from bench press and desk work
indian_alternative: No doorframe? Place hand flat on a wall and rotate body away

name: Deep Breathing
breathing_cue: Inhale 4 counts through nose, hold 2 counts, exhale 6 counts through mouth
coaching_cues: Stand or sit comfortably; place one hand on chest, one on belly; belly should rise on inhale; slow controlled exhales
common_mistakes: Shallow chest breathing; rushing the exhale; not relaxing shoulders
pro_tip: Box breathing (4-4-4-4) activates parasympathetic recovery — perfect end to any workout
indian_alternative: Similar to pranayama basics — the foundation of breath control

name: Kas Glute Bridge
breathing_cue: Exhale at the top, inhale on the descent
coaching_cues: Keep toes raised off the floor to bias glutes over quads
Push through the heel; squeeze hard at the top for 2 seconds
Keep shins vertical; do NOT roll the pelvis — pure hip extension
common_mistakes: Letting knees cave inward
Using lower back instead of glutes at lockout
Going too fast — tempo is critical here
warmup_protocol: 1×20 bodyweight before weighted sets
pro_tip: Elevate upper back on a bench and add a barbell for the loaded version; the hip-extension ROM doubles

name: B-Stance RDL
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you drive the hips
coaching_cues: Front foot takes 90% of the load; back toe lightly touches for balance only
Hinge at the hip — chest leads, hips go back
Feel the stretch in the working hamstring at the bottom
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Letting the back foot bear too much weight
Squatting instead of hinging
warmup_protocol: 1×10 per side BW Romanian hinge
pro_tip: Ideal for home training — a single DB in each hand gives unilateral hip-hinge stimulus without a barbell

name: Cable Pull-Through
breathing_cue: Exhale forcefully as hips snap forward
coaching_cues: Face away from the cable; rope between legs
Hinge aggressively — push hips back until you feel hamstring stretch
Drive hips through — think kettlebell swing, not squat
common_mistakes: Squatting down instead of hinging back
Using arm strength to pull — arms stay passive
Hyperextending the lower back at lockout
warmup_protocol: 2×10 very light, focus on hip-hinge pattern
pro_tip: Low cable = more glute; higher cable = more hamstring. Adjust for your weak point

name: Hip Abductor Machine
breathing_cue: Exhale on the push outward
coaching_cues: Sit tall; keep core braced; avoid rocking the torso
Full ROM — push as wide as the machine allows
Controlled return — don't let the weights slam
common_mistakes: Using momentum — slow and controlled every rep
Tilting the torso to compensate for limited ROM
Skipping the hold at full abduction
warmup_protocol: 1×20 light before working sets
pro_tip: Finish with a 30-second isometric hold at full abduction — nasty glute burn and great for hypertrophy

name: Frog Pumps
breathing_cue: Continuous breathing; exhale at each peak contraction
coaching_cues: Lie on back; soles of feet together, knees flared wide like a frog
Drive hips straight up — the frog position externally rotates to hit the upper glute fibres
Squeeze hard at the top; pause briefly before descending
common_mistakes: Pushing feet apart instead of keeping soles together
Using lower back — squeeze glutes before you lift
Going too shallow on the hip extension
warmup_protocol: No warm-up needed; can be used as activation
pro_tip: Perfect glute activation drill before squats or deadlifts — 25 reps fires up the upper glute fibres that bridges miss

name: High Box Step-Up
breathing_cue: Exhale as you step up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Box height should have knee at ~90° when foot is planted — higher box = more glute
Drive through the heel of the working leg; don't push off the back foot
Stand fully tall at the top before stepping back down
common_mistakes: Pushing off the trailing leg — defeats the purpose
Box too low — becomes more of a lunge than a step-up
Knee caving inward on the drive up
warmup_protocol: 1×10 BW each side on lower box
pro_tip: Hold dumbbells at sides to load without needing a barbell; works equally well at home with a sturdy chair or steps

name: Deficit Reverse Lunge
breathing_cue: Inhale as you step back and lower, exhale as you drive up
coaching_cues: Stand on a 2-4 inch platform to increase ROM at the bottom
Step back far enough for the knee to nearly touch the floor
Keep torso upright — resist the urge to lean forward
common_mistakes: Step too short — front knee travels excessively over the toe
Allowing torso to fold forward under load
Rushing the eccentric — slow the descent to 3 seconds
warmup_protocol: 1×10 BW reverse lunges without deficit
pro_tip: Add a slight forward lean (10°) if your goal is glute development; stay upright for quad dominance

name: Stiff-Legged Deadlift
breathing_cue: Inhale and brace at the top, exhale after lockout
coaching_cues: Keep legs almost fully extended — slight soft bend at knee, NOT bent
Bar travels down the shins; hinge until you feel max hamstring stretch
Drive hips forward to return; squeeze glutes hard at lockout
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back — brace the core hard throughout
Bending the knees into a regular deadlift position
Bar drifting forward away from the body
warmup_protocol: 2×10 at 50% with focus on hamstring stretch
pro_tip: Elevate the bar 1-2 inches on plates if hamstring flexibility limits depth — safer than rounding

name: Standing Single Leg Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl the heel toward your glute
coaching_cues: Attach ankle strap to low cable; stand facing the stack
Keep the working knee aligned with the standing knee — don't flare it
Control the extension; don't let the weight snap the leg straight
common_mistakes: Swinging the hip to complete the rep
Not fully extending the leg on the eccentric
Using too much weight — hamstrings are strong, but isolation requires control
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light for joint warm-up
pro_tip: Single-leg version addresses side-to-side hamstring imbalances that prone leg curl misses; great rehab and prehab tool

name: Decline Dumbbell Press
breathing_cue: Inhale on the descent, exhale on the press
coaching_cues: Set feet securely on the pad; 15-30° decline angle
DBs at chest level, not shoulders — the decline already shifts the vector
Press to full extension but don't lose chest tension at lockout
common_mistakes: Excessive decline — over 45° causes shoulder discomfort
Letting DBs drift toward the head
Rushing the eccentric phase
warmup_protocol: 2×12 at 60% with lighter DBs
pro_tip: Decline angle shifts the peak-contraction point lower on the chest — better lower-pec stretch than flat bench

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
breathing_cue: Inhale as arms open, exhale as they come together
coaching_cues: Slight permanent bend in the elbow — DO NOT straighten arms
Open wide enough for a strong pec stretch; stop before shoulder discomfort
Think 'hugging a barrel' — arc motion, not a pressing motion
common_mistakes: Straightening elbows — converts fly to press, removes pec stretch
Going too heavy — the fly is a stretch exercise, not a strength move
Bouncing at the bottom — high injury risk
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light for shoulder mobility
pro_tip: Use as a pre-exhaustion move before incline press — the pump will be intense

name: Deficit Push-Up
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down to full depth, exhale on the push
coaching_cues: Hands on push-up handles, books, or parallettes — feet on a flat surface
Lower until chest is well below hand level for maximum pec stretch
Elbows at 45° — not flared wide, not tucked tight
common_mistakes: Hands too close together — reduces chest ROM
Sagging hips — maintain a rigid plank from head to heel
Bouncing at the bottom of the stretch
warmup_protocol: 1×10 standard push-ups before deficit version
pro_tip: The extra few centimetres of ROM at the bottom are where the majority of the hypertrophy stimulus lives — this is a bodyweight DB fly equivalent
indian_alternative: Use two thick books or stacked water bottles as handles

name: Floor Press
breathing_cue: Inhale on the descent, exhale on the press
coaching_cues: Lie on the floor; upper arms rest on the floor at the bottom of each rep
Elbows stop at floor — never bounce; pause 1 second before pressing
Excellent for shoulder safety — limited ROM removes the risky stretched position
common_mistakes: Letting elbows slam to the floor rather than softly touching
Arching the lower back excessively off the floor
Using bench-press grip width — go slightly narrower for floor press
warmup_protocol: 2×10 at 60% working weight
pro_tip: Floor press is the best home-gym chest exercise with no bench — perfect tricep and chest strength builder that spares the shoulder
indian_alternative: No bench required — the floor is the bench

name: Machine Lateral Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale on the lift, inhale on the controlled lower
coaching_cues: Set the arm pad just below the elbow — not on the wrist
Slight forward lean on the machine targets the lateral delt more precisely
Lead with the elbow, not the wrist — think 'push elbow up to the ceiling'
common_mistakes: Going too heavy and shrugging — trap dominance will mask delt work
Not reaching full lateral height — 90° or slightly above
Jerking the weight up with momentum
warmup_protocol: 1×20 very light to warm up the rotator cuff
pro_tip: Machine allows constant tension through the full arc — superior to dumbbell for lateral delt isolation at high reps

name: Cable Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise your arm, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Attach a bar or handle to a low cable; stand facing away
Raise arm to shoulder height — going higher increases trap and neck recruitment
Slight elbow bend; keep the arm aligned with the front delt angle (30° off sagittal)
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to initiate the raise
Raising beyond 90° — diminishing returns and higher impingement risk
Letting the weight pull the arm straight back — control the eccentric
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light
pro_tip: Cable version keeps tension on the front delt at the bottom — dumbbell version doesn't. Better for the lengthened-position stimulus

name: Egyptian Lateral Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale on the raise, slow exhale on the 3-second lower
coaching_cues: Stand sideways to a low cable; hold a fixed support with the other hand and lean away
The tilt increases the ROM in the lengthened position — peak stretch at the bottom
Raise the arm in the scapular plane (30° forward) — not directly sideways
common_mistakes: Not leaning far enough — the lean is what makes the lengthened-position superior
Going too fast on the eccentric — the slow lower is where the growth signal lives
Arm drifting in front of the body — stay in the scapular plane
warmup_protocol: 1×15 standard cable lateral raise before attempting
pro_tip: The research-backed 'best' lateral raise variant — lengthened-position tension is 2× more hypertrophic than dumbbell laterals for the same reps

name: Bench Dips
breathing_cue: Inhale on the dip down, exhale on the press up
coaching_cues: Hands shoulder-width on the bench edge; hips close to the bench
Elbows point backward — not flared — to keep tension on the triceps
Lower until upper arm is parallel to the floor; don't go below 90° shoulder
common_mistakes: Dipping too deep — causes shoulder impingement
Elbows flaring sideways — shifts load off triceps
Hips drifting far out — increases shoulder stress
warmup_protocol: 1×10 very light at shallow depth
pro_tip: Elevate feet on another bench to increase loading; add a plate on the thighs for extra resistance — great bodyweight tricep builder
indian_alternative: Use a sturdy chair or low wall

name: Dumbbell Kickback
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend the arm back fully
coaching_cues: Upper arm locked parallel to the floor and torso — ONLY the forearm moves
Extend fully — the tricep contracts hardest in the extended-arm position
Hinge forward 45-60° and brace the core to protect the lower back
common_mistakes: Upper arm dropping — loses tension on the tricep entirely
Swinging the weight with shoulder momentum
Not achieving full elbow extension — partial reps underutilise the long head
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light to warm up the elbow joint
pro_tip: Supinate (rotate palm up) at full extension for a harder tricep contraction — a 10% strength boost for free

name: Overhead Cable Extension
breathing_cue: Inhale on the stretch overhead, exhale on extension
coaching_cues: Face away from the stack; grab rope overhead with both hands behind the head
Keep elbows pointing directly upward — don't let them flare outward
Full extension above the head; feel the long head stretch at the bottom
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring out wide — removes long-head focus
Arching the lower back — engage core tightly
Using too much weight and sacrificing the stretch at the bottom
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light to warm up elbow and shoulder
pro_tip: The overhead position maximally stretches the long head of the tricep — 30% more growth stimulus than pushdowns for the same reps according to recent research

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
breathing_cue: Inhale on the descent, exhale hard on the press
coaching_cues: Grip just inside shoulder width — narrower than bench press but NOT touching
Elbows track close to the torso; elbow angle 20-30° from the body
Bar touches lower chest — NOT the same touch point as bench press
common_mistakes: Grip too narrow — wrist strain and reduced force output
Elbows flaring wide — converts to a chest exercise
Partial reps at the top — full lockout is where tricep finishes the rep
warmup_protocol: 2×10 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: One of the best strength builders for the tricep — can carry over 10-15kg to regular bench press by fixing a tricep-weak lockout

name: Rope Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up
coaching_cues: Neutral (thumbs-up) grip throughout — do NOT supinate
Elbows pinned to sides; only the forearm moves
Squeeze hard at the top; control the cable on the way down
common_mistakes: Supinating at the top — that would make it a standard curl, not hammer
Elbows drifting forward — loses brachialis tension
Too much wrist flexion at the top
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light
pro_tip: The brachialis lies under the bicep — building it pushes the bicep peak up. Rope hammers are the most efficient way to isolate it

name: High Cable Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you flex the bicep toward your ear
coaching_cues: Set cables at head height; face the cable stack; curl toward your ears
Upper arm stays parallel to the floor — elbows fixed in space
Feel the bicep stretch at the start (arm extended forward) and squeeze at peak contraction
common_mistakes: Elbow dropping below head height — loses the lengthened-position advantage
Using both arms asymmetrically — if using two cables, keep motion symmetrical
Jerking the curl — smooth constant tension is the goal
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light
pro_tip: High-cable curl is the lengthened-position bicep exercise — the stretch under load is where hypertrophy research says growth is maximised

name: Pendlay Row
breathing_cue: Inhale and brace before each rep; exhale after each rep reset
coaching_cues: Bar starts on the floor each rep — true dead-stop row (no bounce)
Torso nearly horizontal (10-20° above parallel) at the start
Explosive pull to lower chest; bar path is nearly vertical
common_mistakes: Torso angle too upright — becomes a partial barbell row, not a Pendlay
Not resetting to the floor each rep — removes the strict dead-stop stimulus
Lower back rounding — brace hard before every pull
warmup_protocol: 2×8 at 50% working weight
pro_tip: The dead-stop teaches pure hip-hinge and back strength with zero momentum — 5 kg more on Pendlay Row adds 10 kg to your deadlift over a training cycle

name: Machine High Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as arms extend overhead
coaching_cues: Chest pad supports the torso; pull handles down toward the upper chest
Lead with the elbows; think 'elbows to pockets' — not hands to chest
Full stretch at the top — let the lats lengthen completely before each rep
common_mistakes: Pulling with biceps instead of driving elbows down
Not getting full overhead stretch — the lengthened position matters most
Leaning back excessively — keep chest on the pad
warmup_protocol: 1×15 light to prime lat-bicep connection
pro_tip: The chest-supported position removes lower back from the equation — great for high-volume lat work when the lower back is fatigued from deadlifts

name: Machine Low Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you row, inhale as you extend
coaching_cues: Chest on pad; pull handles toward the lower abdomen, elbows close to the body
Retract scapulae at the back of the movement — squeeze shoulder blades together
Controlled full stretch forward — don't lose the mid-back tension
common_mistakes: Shrugging the traps instead of retracting the scapulae
Bouncing out of the stretched position — slow, controlled eccentric
Pulling too high — row to navel, not to chest
warmup_protocol: 1×15 light for shoulder and mid-back activation
pro_tip: Closer neutral grip hits the mid-back rhomboids and traps harder; wider pronated grip shifts emphasis to the lats. Use both across your training week

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
breathing_cue: Exhale as you push the bar down toward your thighs
coaching_cues: Arms stay straight the ENTIRE movement — this is NOT a lat pulldown
Hinge slightly at the hips; pull the bar in a sweeping arc from overhead to thighs
Think 'armpits to pockets' — this movement is pure lat without bicep interference
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — converts to a lat pulldown and removes the isolation
Using too much weight and swinging the torso
Not reaching full overhead stretch at the start
warmup_protocol: 1×15 very light to feel the lat-shoulder connection
pro_tip: Best pure lat isolation exercise — zero bicep involvement. If you want to feel your lats without bicep fatigue, this is it

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise the legs, inhale on the lower
coaching_cues: Back flat against the pad; arms pressing down into the supports
Posterior pelvic tilt — tuck the pelvis BEFORE lifting; this switches hip flexors off
Raise knees to 90° for beginner; straight-leg raise for advanced
common_mistakes: Swinging the legs with momentum — slow controlled reps only
Not tilting the pelvis — most of the work goes to hip flexors instead of abs
Lower back arching away from the pad
warmup_protocol: 1×10 knee raises before straight-leg version
pro_tip: Add a twist at the top to target obliques — brings knee toward the opposite elbow at peak contraction

name: V-Ups
breathing_cue: Exhale sharply as you fold up into the V position
coaching_cues: Start lying flat; simultaneously raise straight legs and straight arms to meet
Reach fingers toward toes at the peak; spine should form a deep C-curve
Control the return — do NOT slam back to the floor
common_mistakes: Bending the knees — makes the exercise significantly easier, removes load
Using momentum to swing up rather than a controlled abdominal crunch
Dropping back fast — the eccentric is where abdominal strength is built
warmup_protocol: 1×10 regular crunches to activate abs first
pro_tip: Harder than it looks — if lower back arches or you cannot keep legs straight, regress to tuck V-ups first

name: Flutter Kicks
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily throughout; exhale every few kicks
coaching_cues: Lie on back; lift both feet 6 inches off the floor
Alternate small quick kicks; lower back pressed firmly to the floor throughout
Point toes to keep tension on the core and hip flexors
common_mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor — reduces core demand and risks injury
Lifting feet too high — makes it easier; stay low at 6 inches
Holding the breath — breathe rhythmically
warmup_protocol: Not required; can be used as active warm-up
pro_tip: Lower Abs Superset: flutter kicks 30s → leg raise 10 reps → rest 60s. Devastating lower-abdominal burnout circuit

name: Side Plank
breathing_cue: Breathe slowly and steadily throughout the hold
coaching_cues: Elbow directly below the shoulder; body forms a straight diagonal line
Lift the hips high — do NOT sag; squeeze the oblique to keep the position
Stack feet or stagger them for stability; raise the top arm for extra challenge
common_mistakes: Hips sagging below the line — defeats the purpose
Neck craning upward — keep it neutral, in line with the spine
Elbow placed too far from under the shoulder — makes it unstable
warmup_protocol: Not required; great as an activation drill
pro_tip: Add a hip dip (controlled tap to the floor and back up) to make it dynamic — transforms a static hold into a loaded oblique movement

name: Wall Sit
breathing_cue: Breathe normally throughout the hold
coaching_cues: Feet shoulder-width apart
Back flat against wall
Thighs parallel to floor
Hold position
common_mistakes: Leaning forward
Knees caving inward
Feet too close to wall
warmup_protocol: Light leg swings and bodyweight squats
pro_tip: Drive heels into floor to maintain position

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge forward, exhale as you return
coaching_cues: Hands behind head or on hips
Soft bend in knees
Hinge at hips, not waist
Feel stretch in hamstrings
common_mistakes: Rounding the back
Bending too deep at knees
Moving too fast
warmup_protocol: Hip circles and dynamic leg swings
pro_tip: Focus on the hip hinge movement pattern to protect your lower back

name: Doorframe Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Stand in doorframe
Grip frame at hip height
Lean back at 45 degrees
Curl body up using biceps
common_mistakes: Using momentum
Not leaning back enough
Gripping too high
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and wrist rotations
pro_tip: Lean further back to increase difficulty

name: Towel Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Loop towel around a sturdy door handle
Lean back keeping body straight
Pull chest toward door
Squeeze shoulder blades at top
common_mistakes: Hips sagging
Using only arms
Leaning too far from door
warmup_protocol: Cat-cow stretches and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: The further your feet are from the door, the harder the row

name: Negative Pull Up
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower slowly
coaching_cues: Jump or step to top position
Start with chin above bar
Lower yourself as slowly as possible
5-10 seconds down
common_mistakes: Dropping too fast
Not using full range
Not engaging lats
warmup_protocol: Dead hangs and scapular pulls
pro_tip: Control the eccentric to build pulling strength for full pull-ups

name: Glute Kickback
breathing_cue: Exhale as you kick back, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: On hands and knees
Keep core tight
Kick leg back and up
Squeeze glute at top
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips
Arching lower back
Not squeezing at peak
warmup_protocol: Hip circles and glute bridges
pro_tip: Add ankle weight or resistance band to increase difficulty

name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hold dumbbells at sides
Rise on balls of feet
Full range at top and bottom
Control the descent
common_mistakes: Bouncing at bottom
Partial range of motion
Leaning forward
warmup_protocol: Ankle rotations and light calf stretches
pro_tip: Stand on a step edge for greater range of motion

name: Split Squat
breathing_cue: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you rise
coaching_cues: Staggered stance, rear foot elevated or flat
Lower back knee toward floor
Keep front shin vertical
Drive through front heel to rise
common_mistakes: Front knee caving
Leaning too far forward
Rising on toes of front foot
warmup_protocol: Hip flexor stretches and leg swings
pro_tip: Elevate rear foot on a bench to increase range (Bulgarian split squat)

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
breathing_cue: Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Set bench to 30-45 degree incline
Press dumbbells up and slightly together
Control the descent
Full range of motion at bottom
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows too wide
Bouncing off chest
Uneven press
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and light dumbbell presses
pro_tip: Keep a slight arch in lower back for shoulder safety

name: Bodyweight Rear Delt Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down on the floor or a bench
Arms out to the sides in a T, thumbs up
Squeeze shoulder blades to lift the arms
Keep the neck neutral and chin tucked
common_mistakes: Shrugging the traps
Using momentum to swing the arms
Lifting the chest off the floor
warmup_protocol: Band pull-aparts and arm circles
pro_tip: Go light and slow — the rear delts respond to the squeeze, not the load

name: Elevated Pike Push Up
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press away
coaching_cues: Feet on a chair, sofa or low step; hips stacked high over the shoulders
Head travels toward the floor between the hands, not forward
Elbows track back at roughly 45 degrees, not flared wide
Press until the elbows lock, keeping the hips high throughout
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop into a plank, which turns it into a push-up
Looking forward and craning the neck
Using a surface so high the wrists cannot stay flat
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and wrist rotations
pro_tip: The higher the feet, the closer this gets to a handstand push-up. Raise the surface before you add reps.

name: Prone Reverse Snow Angel
breathing_cue: Breathe steadily; do not hold your breath at the top
coaching_cues: Lie face-down, forehead resting on the floor
Arms start by the hips, palms facing down
Sweep the arms out and overhead just above the floor, then back
Keep the arms straight and the ribs down the whole way
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest and arching the lower back to help the arms
Bending the elbows as the arms pass shoulder height
Rushing. The whole point is the slow sweep.
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and cat-cow
pro_tip: If the arms will not pass the shoulders, stop there. The range comes back as the mid-back wakes up.

name: Table Row
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie under a sturdy table and grip the edge at chest width
Body straight from heel to head, heels on the floor
Pull the chest to the underside of the table
Lower under control until the arms are straight
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag so the pull becomes a shrug
Using a light folding table that tips. Check it takes your weight first.
Pulling with the arms and never squeezing the shoulder blades
warmup_protocol: Band pull-aparts or scapular shrugs
pro_tip: Bend the knees to make it easier, or put the heels on a chair to make it harder.

name: Prone Lat Pull
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the elbows down, inhale as you reach
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the arms straight overhead in a Y
Lift the hands slightly off the floor and hold them there
Pull the elbows down and back toward the ribs, squeezing the lats
Reach the arms overhead again without letting the hands touch down
common_mistakes: Resting the hands on the floor between reps, which kills the tension
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Arching the lower back instead of moving at the shoulder
warmup_protocol: Cat-cow and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: This is the vertical pull you can do on a hotel floor. Squeeze for a full second at the bottom.

name: Sliding Lat Pull
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull yourself forward
coaching_cues: Kneel on a smooth floor with both hands on a folded towel in front of you
Slide the towel forward until the arms are overhead and the chest is low
Pull the towel back toward the knees using the lats, not the hips
Keep the ribs down so the lower back does not take over
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop and the back arch at full reach
Pushing back with the legs instead of pulling with the lats
Trying it on carpet, where the towel will not slide
warmup_protocol: Dead bugs and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: Reach only as far as you can keep the ribs down. The range grows with the mid-section, not the shoulder.

name: Doorway Isometric Lat Pull
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand in a doorway and reach both hands high onto the frame
Pull down and in against the frame as if driving the elbows to the ribs
Build to full effort over two seconds, then hold
Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears
common_mistakes: Jerking into full force instead of building into it
Holding the breath, which spikes blood pressure
Hanging off the frame rather than pulling against it
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and band pull-aparts
pro_tip: An isometric builds the mind-muscle link a beginner is missing. It is how you start owning your own bodyweight overhead.

name: Self-Resisted Bicep Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Place the free hand on top of the working wrist
Curl the working arm up while the free hand pushes back against it
Resist hard on the way down. The lowering is where the work is.
Keep the working elbow pinned to the ribs
common_mistakes: Pushing so hard nothing moves. It should still travel.
Letting the working elbow drift forward
Giving up the resistance on the lowering half
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: Go easy on the way up and fight hard on the way down. The negative is what a bodyweight curl has to offer.

name: Towel Bicep Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Stand on one end of a towel and hold the other in one hand
Curl upward while pressing down through the standing foot
Keep the elbow tight to the ribs and the wrist neutral
Lower slowly against the same tension
common_mistakes: Leaning back to help the arm up
Letting the towel go slack at the bottom
Gripping so hard the forearm fails before the bicep
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: Shorten your grip on the towel to increase the tension. It is your load selector.

name: Self-Resisted Triceps Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Working arm overhead, hand behind the head
Free hand grips the working wrist and resists as you straighten the arm
Keep the working elbow pointing at the ceiling, close to the head
Resist on the way back down as well
common_mistakes: Letting the working elbow flare out to the side
Only resisting on the way up
Shrugging the shoulder to get the arm overhead
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: If the shoulder will not let the arm sit overhead, do it with the arm across the chest instead.

name: Wall Triceps Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you press away from the wall
coaching_cues: Stand an arm-length from a wall, forearms flat against it, elbows at shoulder height
Body straight from heel to head; lean in until the forehead nears the wall
Press back to straight arms using the triceps only
Keep the elbows pointing forward, never flaring out
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift wide, which hands the work to the chest
Bending at the hips instead of holding a straight line
Standing too close, which removes most of the range
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: Step the feet further back to make it harder. This is the wall version of a skull crusher.

name: Prone Y Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down, arms overhead in a Y, thumbs pointing up
Raise the arms as high as the shoulder blades allow
Keep the forehead down and the neck long
Lower slowly rather than dropping
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and compressing the neck
Shrugging the traps to get the arms higher
Arching the lower back to fake the range
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and cat-cow
pro_tip: Height is not the goal. A low, controlled raise with the traps quiet beats a high one with them loud.

name: Towel Lateral Raise
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut in front of you at hip height, one end in each hand
Pull outward against the towel and raise the arms to shoulder height
Hold the outward tension for the whole set
Keep the shoulders down and the elbows soft
common_mistakes: Letting the towel go slack at the top
Raising above shoulder height, which brings the traps in
Holding the breath during the isometric
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: Widen your grip on the towel for less tension, narrow it for more.

name: Prone T Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down, arms straight out to the sides in a T
Thumbs up; lift the arms by squeezing the shoulder blades together
Hold the top for a full second before lowering
Keep the forehead down and the ribs on the floor
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest to make the arms travel further
Shrugging the traps up toward the ears
Bending the elbows once it gets hard
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and cat-cow
pro_tip: If you can hold the top for a second, the mid-back is doing it. If you cannot, the momentum was.

name: Doorway Isometric Row
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand facing a doorway and grip both sides of the frame at chest height
Lean the hips back until the arms are straight and the body is angled
Pull the chest toward the frame and hold at the top
Squeeze the shoulder blades together for the whole hold
common_mistakes: Standing too upright, which removes the load
Pulling with the arms while the shoulder blades stay still
Letting the hips sag forward out of the straight line
warmup_protocol: Band pull-aparts or scapular shrugs
pro_tip: Walk the feet forward to increase the lean and the difficulty.

name: Standing Towel Pull Apart
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the towel apart
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut at shoulder height, hands wider than the shoulders
Pull outward against the towel and draw the hands apart and back
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end of the pull
Return slowly, keeping the towel under tension throughout
common_mistakes: Letting the towel go slack between reps
Arching the lower back to get more range
Leading with the hands instead of the shoulder blades
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: This is the band pull-apart for people who own no band. Narrow the grip for more tension.

name: Prone W Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the elbows bent, arms forming a W beside the ribs
Drive the elbows back and up, squeezing the shoulder blades down
Keep the wrists in line with the forearms
Lower slowly without resting the arms on the floor
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift up toward the head, which recruits the traps
Lifting the chin and compressing the neck
Resting between reps, which kills the tension
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and cat-cow
pro_tip: The W hits the lower traps harder than the T. Alternate them week to week.

name: Towel Lat Pulldown
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as you reach up
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut overhead, hands wider than the shoulders
Pull outward against the towel and bring it down behind the head
Drive the elbows toward the ribs, not just the hands down
Press back overhead against the same tension
common_mistakes: Letting the towel slacken, which removes all resistance
Bringing it down in front instead of behind, which becomes a shrug
Leaning back to fake the range
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and arm circles
pro_tip: Keep pulling out on the towel the whole set. The tension is the load.

name: Wall Lat Press
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand side-on to a wall with the near arm straight and the palm flat on it
Press the palm DOWN the wall as if pulling yourself up past it
Feel the lat under the armpit engage and hold
Keep the shoulder pulled away from the ear
common_mistakes: Pressing into the wall rather than down it
Shrugging the shoulder up as effort rises
Holding the breath through the contraction
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and cat-cow
pro_tip: A wall is always there. This teaches the lat what to do before there is a bar to do it on.

name: Prone Lat Pull Hold
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the arms overhead and the hands off the floor
Pull the elbows down to the ribs and HOLD there
Keep the chest lightly off the floor and the neck long
Squeeze as if trying to bend a bar down through the whole hold
common_mistakes: Letting the hands drop to the floor mid-hold
Arching hard through the lower back instead of the upper
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
warmup_protocol: Cat-cow and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: The hold builds what the rep cannot: time under tension with nothing to hang from.

name: Towel Hammer Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Stand on one end of a towel, holding the other with a neutral (thumb-up) grip
Curl upward while pressing down through the standing foot
Keep the elbow pinned to the ribs and the thumb up throughout
Lower slowly against the same tension
common_mistakes: Rotating the palm up, which turns it back into a standard curl
Leaning back to help the arm
Letting the towel go slack at the bottom
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: The neutral grip shifts the work to the brachialis, which is what adds width to the arm.

name: Doorway Isometric Curl
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Stand in a doorway with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and the palm under the frame
Press up into the frame as if curling it, building over two seconds
Keep the elbow tight to the ribs and the wrist neutral
Hold at full effort, then release slowly
common_mistakes: Jerking into full force instead of building into it
Letting the shoulder rise to help the arm press
Holding the breath, which spikes blood pressure
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: Do one hold at 90 degrees and one just below it. An isometric only trains the angle you hold.

name: Table Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Sit under a sturdy table and grip its edge with palms facing you
Keep the elbows tight to the ribs and pull the chest up toward your hands
Drive with the biceps rather than the shoulder blades
Lower under control until the arms are straight
common_mistakes: Rowing with the back instead of curling with the arms
Using a table that tips. Check it takes your weight first.
Letting the elbows travel forward as you pull
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: Walk the feet out to make it harder, tuck them in to make it easier.

name: Towel Triceps Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return
coaching_cues: Hold one end of a towel overhead, the other behind the back in the opposite hand
Straighten the top arm against the resistance of the bottom hand
Keep the top elbow pointing at the ceiling, close to the head
Let the bottom hand resist on the way back down as well
common_mistakes: Letting the top elbow flare out to the side
Only resisting in one direction
Pulling so hard with the bottom hand that nothing moves
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: The bottom hand is your weight stack. Ease off it to add reps, pull harder to add load.

name: Elevated Diamond Push Up
breathing_cue: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press
coaching_cues: Hands in a diamond on a chair, step or low table; feet on the floor
Elbows stay close to the ribs, not flared out
Lower until the chest touches the hands
Press to a full lockout and squeeze the triceps
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows, which hands the work to the chest
Letting the hips sag out of the straight line
Using a surface that slides. Brace it against a wall.
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: The higher the hands, the easier it is. This is how you work toward a floor diamond push-up.

name: Wall Triceps Press
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Face a wall with the palms flat at chest height and the elbows bent
Press into the wall as if straightening the arms, without moving
Keep the elbows tucked toward the ribs, never flared
Build to full effort over two seconds and hold
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows, which turns it into a chest press
Leaning the body weight in instead of pressing with the arms
Holding the breath through the effort
warmup_protocol: Wrist rotations and arm circles
pro_tip: Set the elbow angle before you press. The angle you hold is the angle you train.

name: Towel Front Raise
breathing_cue: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Hold a towel taut in front of the thighs, one end in each hand
Pull outward against it and raise the arms to shoulder height
Keep the elbows soft and the shoulders down
Lower slowly, holding the outward tension the whole way
common_mistakes: Swinging the towel up with the hips
Raising above shoulder height, which brings the traps in
Letting the towel slacken at the bottom
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: Narrow the grip for more tension. That is your only load selector here.

name: Wall Shoulder Slide
breathing_cue: Exhale as you slide up, inhale as you come down
coaching_cues: Stand with the back, head and both forearms flat against a wall
Slide the forearms up the wall without letting them lift off it
Keep the lower back close to the wall; do not let the ribs flare
Come down slowly to just below shoulder height
common_mistakes: Letting the wrists or elbows peel off the wall to get more range
Arching the lower back away from the wall
Shrugging the shoulders up at the top
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and cat-cow
pro_tip: Go only as high as the forearms stay on the wall. The lost range is the point, not the failure.

name: Isometric Lateral Raise
breathing_cue: Breathe normally through the hold. Never hold your breath.
coaching_cues: Raise both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height
Hold there with the palms down and the elbows soft
Keep the shoulders pulled down away from the ears
Hold until the shoulders burn, then lower slowly
common_mistakes: Letting the arms drift forward out of the side plane
Shrugging as fatigue builds
Dropping the arms rather than lowering them
warmup_protocol: Arm circles and shoulder rolls
pro_tip: No load needed. The side delt is small enough that gravity and time are plenty.

name: Prone Shoulder Extension
breathing_cue: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie face-down with the arms straight beside the hips, palms facing in
Lift the hands toward the ceiling, keeping the arms straight
Squeeze at the top with the shoulders pulled down
Lower slowly without letting the hands rest on the floor
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows to get the hands higher
Lifting the chest to add range
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
warmup_protocol: Shoulder rolls and cat-cow
pro_tip: Small range, big squeeze. Two inches done properly beats six done with the back.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
breathing_cue: Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Lie on your back, one foot planted, the other leg extended
Drive through the planted heel until the hips are level with the knee and shoulder
Squeeze the glute hard at the top for a full second
Keep the hips square. Do not let the free side drop.
common_mistakes: Letting the free hip sag, which hides the weak side
Pushing through the toes instead of the heel
Arching the lower back at the top instead of squeezing the glute
warmup_protocol: Glute bridges and dead bugs
pro_tip: If the hamstring cramps, walk the heel closer to the hips. That is a leverage problem, not a weakness.

name: Sliding Leg Curl
breathing_cue: Exhale as you pull the heels in
coaching_cues: Lie on your back on a smooth floor with both heels on a folded towel
Bridge the hips up and hold them there for the whole set
Slide the heels out until the legs are almost straight
Pull the heels back in using the hamstrings, hips staying high
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop as the legs extend
Sliding out further than you can pull back
Trying it on carpet, where the towel will not slide
warmup_protocol: Glute bridges and leg swings
pro_tip: Cramping hamstrings mean the range was too long, not that you are done. Shorten it.

name: Elevated Single Leg Hip Thrust
breathing_cue: Exhale as you drive up, inhale as you lower
coaching_cues: Upper back resting on a chair or sofa edge, one foot planted
Other leg tucked or extended; drive through the planted heel
Finish with the hips level and the ribs down, not flared
Lower under control until the hips are just off the floor
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of squeezing the glute
Letting the planted foot drift too far forward, which recruits the hamstring
Using a surface that slides out from under you
warmup_protocol: Glute bridges and hip circles
pro_tip: The chair adds range the floor cannot. That range is where the glute actually grows.

name: Standing Single Leg Hinge
breathing_cue: Inhale as you hinge, exhale as you stand
coaching_cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, arms reaching forward
Hinge at the hip, sending the free leg straight back as a counterweight
Keep the back flat and the hips square to the floor
Stand by driving the hip forward, not by pulling with the back
common_mistakes: Rotating the free hip open, which turns it into a twist
Rounding the back to reach lower
Locking the standing knee
warmup_protocol: Leg swings and glute bridges
pro_tip: Touch a wall with your fingertips for balance. Balance failing first hides how much hamstring you have.
